pr_title: lib: json: Decoding of partially-recognized keys
pr_body:
IMO, the JSON library should be able to parse a JSON that contains known as well as unknown fields. These two tests verify that behaviour.

Fixes #55758
pr_comments: @martinjaeger Thanks for the review, I incorporated your suggestions and rebased.

Thanks for your PR and bringing this issue back up again.

A fix with a slightly different approach was addressed in PR #47989. The associated issue #47988 contains possible inputs to consider (cf. @M1cha's review above).

(when I say this I mean #55757, when I say that I mean #47989)

> Thanks for your PR and bringing this issue back up again.
> 
> A fix with a slightly different approach was addressed in PR #47989. The associated issue #47988 contains possible inputs to consider (cf. @M1cha's review above).

That approach might be better because if I'm not mistaken, the approach in this PR would accept invalid json like:
```json
{
    "invalid": {{}},
    "valid": 5
}
```

At the same time, this PR would also not accept all valid inputs for the unsupported field, since we keep calling `obj_next` which parses the input as `"field": value` which will stop being true as soon as we enter other types like arrays:
```json
{
    "invalid": {
        "key": [0, 1, 2]
    },
    "valid": 5
}
```

I haven't tested any of these inputs (yet), but my brain compiler tells me these might be an issue.

> At the same time, this PR would also not accept all valid inputs for the unsupported field, since we keep calling `obj_next` which parses the input as `"field": value` which will stop being true as soon as we enter other types like arrays:
> 
> ```json
> {
>     "invalid": {
>         "key": [0, 1, 2]
>     },
>     "valid": 5
> }
> ```

Is this really the case? The `skip_field()` function in #47989 handles both `JSON_TOK_OBJECT_{START|END}` and `JSON_TOK_ARRAY_{START|END}` tokens and so should correctly handle the input you mention.
